Messages.Author: scrote
Messages.Body:
If I have a Brother's Grimm in play and someone pitches a master to
take it (during their master ohase of course), can I tap cards (such
as dreams of the sphinx, barrens, fragment of the book of Nod, etc...)
to sift for a master to cancel their attempt?

I would think yes, but am not positive.

Thanks,
-scrote

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:


Actually, I think the answer would be no. Unlike "that other game," in VTES
there is no stack or first-in-last-out rule. Unless specified otherwise just
about everything (outside of actions and strikes) happens instantaneously. Once
an effect is played, there is no chance to do something before that happens
(though there is still a chance to cancel that effect).

If someone Golcondas your vampire, you can't interrupt the effect by
Heidelburg'ing blood off and then taking the pool for the Golconda. And if
someone is going to play Anachronism on Masika you can't use the Heidelburg "as
a fast effect" to move your Assault Rifle. When someone contests your Dreams
you can't tap it right before it comes into play b/c there is no timing window
for that.

As soon as the other player uses his master phase (in this case, to steal
Brothers Grimm), you have the chance to cancel the effect (by discarding) but
that's all you can do. You can't "time-out" everything and use other effects
and play cards (though of course you could always do that before his master
phase. Similarly timing issues have existed for quite some time with cards like
Heidelburg).

Note that actions and strikes have delayed effects. So if someone takes the
action to steal the Fragment or Disputed Territory your Barrens, you can tap
the Frag/Barrens before the action is resolved.

Halcyan 2

Not. All you can do here is Sudden or fish for a Sudden.

> "I play Art of Love on your untapped War Ghoul"
> "I tap Fragment to try and get a sudden, I don't get a sudden, you get
> warghoul"
> "I tap War Ghoul to burn your Barrens"
> "I tap Barrens to ....get a card. Ok, War Ghoul burns my tapped
> Barrens"
> Legal or not?

I think legal up to the point that you tap the Barrens. Since
there's no way to keep the now-stolen War Ghoul from burning
the Barrens (ie there is nothing that would cancel it that you
could be fishing for by tapping Barrens), you can't "respond"
to the War Ghoul tap-and-burn effect - once it's announced, it
happens, and anything that anyone else wants to do will happen
*after* the burning, not before it.

> Really, played effects that resolve as played should not be allowed to
> be 'interrupted' by tapping stuff or anything else that doesn't have
> specific 'as played' text.
>
> 'I arson your barrens'
> 'i tap the barrens, and draw a Direct Intervention. I play it to
> cancel the arson as it is played'
> Is it still 'as it is played', or have we moved past that timing point
> by the tapping of the barrens?

Yes, you can do that too. Anything that can be canceled with
Direct Intervention or Sudden Reversal has an "as it is played"
window that exists and card-drawing effects are allowed in that
window.

You're right, though, that it is confusing and inconsistent to
allow card-searching effects in that window. If the window
exists only because of the existence of Sudden Reversal and
Direct Intervention, it makes a lot more sense to not allow
anything else to happen in that window besides the play of
Sudden Reversal or Direct Intervention from hand. Card-
searching effects are not intuitively "faster" than others,
given that VTES is not supposed to have "interrupts" other
than cards with text explicitly telling you that they cancel
things "as played".

Josh

The problem of "quickest draw" already exists, to the
extent that it exists, in a ton of situations. Imagine
that player B is thinking about using Heidelberg Castle
before player A decides whether to use his Temptation
to take control of player B's vampire.

The solution is generally 1.6.1.6 in the rulebook, which
says that the player whose turn it is always gets to use
his or her effect first if more than one player wants to
do something at the same time.

The solution for player B is to decide to Barrens before
player A gets to his master phase. Otherwise, player B
has to ask player A if A wants to do anything, because B
wants to play an effect; A can then say "yeah, I'll
steal your Brothers Grimm".

Does this not seem like a workable system?

Josh
